summary: Tested the Warranty module (backend + UI) using real API flows. New pytest suite test_warranty.py has 31 tests: 26 pass, 5 fail. What works: (1) a fiscal invoice auto-creates exactly 1 certificate, and a proforma creates none. Part lines get the product's warranty_months (12 and the default 24 verified); labor gets 3 months; valid_to is computed with relativedelta. GET /invoices/{id} shows only {id, number, issued_date}, and null for a proforma. (2) The PDF returns 200 application/pdf with Content-Disposition attachment filename=GAR-YYYY-NNNNNN.pdf. It is 1 A4 page, diacritics render correctly (checked visually), the table is readable, and '&'/'<' in descriptions do not break it. It returns 404 when there is no certificate. (3) /warranties correctly separates active/expired/all; expiry was simulated in the DB. (4) Claims: qty 0, negative, or > invoiced, unknown or expired lines, an empty description, empty lines and an invoice without a certificate all return 400 and create no WO. A valid claim creates a DG-* claim plus exactly 1 GAR-* WO (is_warranty, status noua, unit_price 0 on every line, correct client/vehicle, part+labor types). (5) PUT validates all 3 enums (400), returns 404 for a missing or bad id, persists the changes and keeps the invoice_id/work_order_id links. (6) The original WO shows warranty_alerts while coverage is active, and the alert disappears after expiry. RBAC: 401 without a token, 403 for mecanic. UI: the certificate button appears in InvoiceDetail and is absent on the proforma; PDF download works from the invoice and from /warranties; the WO alert banner shows; the claim dialog works end to end (invoice select, coverage lines, checkbox auto-fills qty, Save disabled until valid, toast); the edit dialog persists changes; on mobile at 390px the document width is 390 (no outer overflow), the claims table scrolls inside its own container, and the dialog fits the screen.

critical.issue: The roles receptioner and magazioner have 'warranties' but not 'invoices'. The claim dialog (/invoices?type=fiscal + /warranties/invoices/{id}) and the certificate download return 403 for them, so these roles can see the page but cannot open a claim or download the PDF. Verified with magazie@: GET /warranties is 200, but /warranties/invoices/{id} is 403.

Claimed qty is not cumulative. (a) The same source_line_id repeated in one request passes (2+2 on a line invoiced with qty 2 returns 200). (b) Repeated claims on the same line are accepted indefinitely (1 + 2 > 2 returns 200). Each one creates a new zero-cost WO.

minor.issue: supplier_return_id is not checked (a nonexistent ObjectId is accepted). There is no cross-validation either: technical_result=conform + resolution=admis_rambursat is accepted, and so is supplier_return_status=acceptat without a supplier_return_id. The claim can still be edited after it is closed (resolution final). There is no status history.

Runs after the invoice insert with no try/except. int(None) or a non-numeric warranty_months on a product raises a 500 after the invoice is already saved, leaving an invoice without a certificate. warranty_months=0 (a product with no warranty) is forced to 1 month by max(1, ...). There is no unique index on warranty_certificates.invoice_id.
A full or partial credit note does not cancel or reduce the certificate coverage; the credited lines stay active and can be claimed.

Nothing blocks editing prices or lines, or issuing a fiscal invoice on the GAR WO. A fiscal invoice on it would create a NEW certificate. Its numbering uses the work_order counter with a GAR- prefix, which can be confused with the certificate numbers (also GAR-YYYY-...).

<b> does not render bold: registerFontFamily is missing for WarrantyRoboto. Dates are ISO (2027-10-18), not dd.mm.yyyy. The table has no quantity or product code column, and there is no seller CUI or client address.

ui_bugs.issue: The invoice select lists every fiscal invoice (including credit notes and invoices with no certificate); choosing one without a certificate silently shows nothing (404 with no message).
The title says 'Certificate active' but the list loads status= (all). Expired certificates have no active/expired badge, only '0 acoperiri active'.
The warranty WO has no visual 'Garanție' marker (is_warranty / warranty_claim_number are not used in the frontend), and there is no link from the claim to the WO.

integration_issues.issue: 403 on /invoices and /warranties/invoices/{id}, so the dialog stays empty and the PDF download fails.

issues: The claims table only shows Claim/Invoice/WO/Resolution; technical_result and supplier return status are not visible without opening edit
Native <select> (NativeSelect) instead of shadcn Select in the dialogs

action_items: Give receptioner/magazioner access: allow require('warranties') (or invoices OR warranties) on /warranties/invoices/{id}[/certificate] and add an invoice selection endpoint that lists only invoices with a certificate (e.g. built from GET /warranties)
POST /warranty-claims: aggregate qty per source_line_id in the request and subtract qty already claimed in existing (non-rejected) claims

PUT /warranty-claims: check that supplier_return_id exists in supplier_returns; add cross-validation (conform -> resolution respins/in_analiza; acceptat/trimis -> supplier_return_id required); lock after a final resolution
create_certificate: int(months or 24), allow 0 = no warranty, try/except so invoicing never fails; add a unique index on invoice_id
Storno: mark credited lines as not covered in the certificate
Warranty WO: show a 'Garanție' badge in WorkOrderDetail/WorkOrders, lock prices to 0, do not issue a certificate or charge a fiscal invoice on is_warranty
ClaimDialog: filter invoices to those that have a certificate; show an explicit message when there is no certificate
critical_code_review_comments: routes_warranty.create_claim: line 100 is a single ~600-character line (and line 104 too); hard to maintain
warranty_service: __import__('bson').ObjectId inline; there is a 'from core import oid' already available
Claim creation is not transactional: it consumes 2 counters and inserts the WO before the claim; if the insert fails, the WO stays orphaned
list_warranties loads up to 2000 certificates and filters in Python; there is no index on vehicle_id/invoice_id (used by warranty_alerts and lookups)

success_rate.frontend: ~90% (all main flows OK; RBAC role gap and UX gaps)
